text: Lucy Snowe!” she cried in a somewhat sobbing voice, half hysterical. “What in the world is the matter?” I drily said. “How do I look—how do I look to-night?” she demanded. “As usual,” said I; “preposterously vain.” “Caustic creature! You never have a kind word for me; but in spite of you, and all other envious detractors, I know I am beautiful; I feel it, I see it—for there is a great looking-glass in the dressing-room, where I can view my shape from head to foot.
